transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-09 16:00 PT | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Maya, Ethan, Sofia (Redwood) — Liam, Nora, Priya, Ravi (BlueBasin)

Summary: Quick sprint planning for next 4 weeks of co-sell work, pick pilots, define handoffs and tech checks.

[00:00] Maya: Okay hi everyone, thanks for carving time. I'll kick off, uh, this is Maya from Redwood — our goal today is to land the pilot list and who owns what.
[00:18] Liam: Hey Maya, thanks. Nora and I have reviewed your previous playbook, looks promising, uh, we wanna make sure the routing rules map to our existing partner portal.
[00:30] Maya: Totally. We can map to your portal, two options — API webhook or SFTP batch, though webhook is real time.
[00:42] Nora: Webhook sounds better, but we do need attribution persisted to Salesforce. We also need the partner id to be present.
[00:53] Ethan: (chime) Quick note — we can include partner_id as meta in the proxied request, it shows up in the logs and the console. Small caveat: if you want full audit in your tenancy we can push events to your Kafka/CloudTrail.
[01:10] Priya: When you say "in your tenancy" do you mean the Redwood private offering or hosted?
[01:16] Ethan: Good question — hosted can do partner metadata but the Private/VPC gives you full event streaming into your stack. Hosted is faster to get started.
[01:28] Nora: For the pilot, time is tight, so hosted plus a webhook seems fine. Later we can talk dedicated pools.
[01:37] Maya: Great. On pilots — we recommend 3 accounts to keep the sprint focused. We suggested Acme Fintech, Meridian Health, and EcoPay. Thoughts?
[01:48] Liam: Acme is top priority — they're heavy on latency SLAs and want VPC; Meridian is smaller, compliance heavy (HIPAA-ish), EcoPay is a good commercial win.
[02:02] Ravi: Quick tech note on Acme — they use long context (around 6k tokens) and do reranking with embeddings, so KV cache behavior matters.
[02:15] Ethan: Okay, interesting. Our runtime supports dynamic KV cache and batching, but for 6k flows we should validate memory footprint. I'll prepare a mini-benchmark.
[02:28] Maya: Action: Ethan will run a sample with 6k token seqs, 8 concurrent streams, measure p95 latency.
[02:36] Ethan: Yep, I'll use the perf harness and share outputs.
[02:40] Priya: On the commercial side, can we be explicit about revenue splits for partner-introduced deals?
[02:47] Sofia: We usually default to a 70/30 split for the pilot (partner/redewood?) — oh sorry Redwood — 70 partner, 30 Redwood for introduced & co-led. This is negotiable depending on contribution.
[02:58] Priya: That's in line with our expectations for introductions, but for joint-sourced we'll need to agree on commission waterfall.
[03:06] Maya: We'll draft an MSA addendum for pilot terms and revenue waterfall. I'll circulate.
[03:12] Nora: Also need SSO and SCIM — partners want SAML.
[03:18] Ethan: We support SSO SAML and OIDC; SCIM provisioning is available for customers on dedicated/private. For hosted we can do manual provisioning.
[03:29] Liam: Security checks — do you have SOC2 Type II?
[03:33] Maya: Yes we do, and we can share the compliance pack.
[03:37] Priya: Can you also share pen test and hardening notes?
[03:40] Maya: Sure, will attach the security packet.
[03:43] [04:00] Ravi: (to Priya) for the Acme POC I'll need a small sample dataset and a dev account.
[04:07] Priya: We'll anonymize data and send a subset.
[04:10] Maya: Cool. On lead routing — the main open question: who owns the initial discovery call? BlueBasin AE or Redwood AE?
[04:19] Liam: Our preference is partner owns discovery, Redwood can join as needed. We want to control the initial relationship.
[04:26] Maya: That works; we just ask for joint intro and then Redwood AE will follow. We'll log activity in CRM and attribute.
[04:33] Ethan: Technical handoff best practice — partner books a "technical discovery" with Redwood SEs; we record notes in the shared playbook doc.
[04:41] Maya: Next, timeline — we propose 4-week sprint: week 1 onboarding + security review, week 2 perf validation, week 3 POC run, week 4 wrap + pricing review.
[04:53] Nora: That seems tight but doable. If we get Acme to approve data access quickly we can hit it.
[05:01] Maya: Let's call out dependencies: 1) signed NDA/MSA addendum; 2) sample data provision; 3) access to Acme environment or sample traffic.
[05:11] Priya: On the NDA, legal wants a draft before next Friday.
[05:15] Maya: I'll push the MSA draft today.
[05:18] [05:40] Ethan: On technical validation — two modes: Hosted quick test (spinning up hosted endpoint) vs Dedicated smoke (requires capacity and reserved pool). For pilot we recommend hosted to start.
[05:53] Ravi: If Acme requires VPC then hosted is not acceptable. They asked specifically for private tenancy previously.
[05:59] Maya: Noted. We'll surface a cost delta for private vs hosted. Sofia, can you run a cost/latency estimate?
[06:06] Sofia: Yep, I'll model 50k tokens/day with 3ms p50 vs 80ms p95 and show monthly cost for hosted vs dedicated.
[06:17] Liam: Also: what about data residency? Acme needs EU residency for some flows.
[06:22] Ethan: We can pin region to EU region but full residency in customer VPC only with Private deployment. Hosted EU region keeps data in EU but logs might transit — will confirm.
[06:34] Priya: Please document that.
[06:37] Maya: We'll add a short one-pager on residency constraints.
[06:40] [07:10] (People skim for docs links)
[07:15] Maya: Okay quick risk triage: top risk is legal turn time on MSA, second is Acme's VPC requirement, third is alignment on revenue split.
[07:25] Priya: Agreed. If legal delays, we can run an internal demo while awaiting signature.
[07:30] Ethan: Another small note — embeddings storage and rerankers; if we need sub-second reranking we should consider GPU quant profiles. I'll include recommended quant settings in the benchmark doc.
[07:45] Ravi: Perfect.
[07:48] Maya: Alright, let's capture owners: Maya will share deck+MSA; Ethan will produce perf report; Ravi will run baseline tests; Sofia will do cost sheet; Liam and Nora will coordinate intros to Acme.
[08:00] Nora: We'll target next Tue for the technical validation call.
[08:05] Maya: Scheduling now — is 10am PT on 2026-06-16 okay?
[08:10] Liam: Works.
[08:13] Priya: Works.
[08:16] Maya: Good. Anything else?
[08:20] Priya: One last ask — can Redwood provide a one-page win story template for co-branded case studies?
[08:26] Maya: Yep we'll include a template in the enablement folder.
[08:30] Ethan: I'll also include a minimal perf checklist so SEs have a runbook.
[08:36] Maya: Cool. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifact links and calendar invites.
[08:42] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "clear-on" vs "Clairon"), some punctuation missing, speaker overlap present.
